name: genesispay-catalog
description: Passt: search products at online stores, compare listed prices and stock, and see any discount code a store has published. Read-only.

interface.longDescription:
Passt helps you find products and published discount codes at online stores, from your chat. Its catalog is the Passt index. Look a product up by words, category, store, currency and price range, sort by price or newest, and see each result's listed price, availability and picture as the index last read it from the store. In ChatGPT the offers appear as a swipeable card with up to eight products, cheapest first within comparable offers, with pictures and, for clothing and shoes, the sizes the store lists; you can filter by size. For a broad request such as "a pullover" it first asks one short round of neutral questions (for whom, colour, size, budget) and then searches. List the stores the index has seen with a UCP business profile, with their product counts and measured uptime, or see which products appeared in the last seven days.

Where a store has published a discount code, the result shows it. Many stores have not, and the plugin never guesses or invents a code.

It only reads public catalog data. It needs no login or account, cannot reach your data, and cannot buy, pay or prepare a payment. Every purchase happens on the store's own website. Some links are affiliate links and are marked. Commission plays no role in how results are ordered, but the index reads some stores' catalogs more often than others, prioritising stores in Passt's affiliate programmes, so those stores may show more products. Text written by stores is passed on as written and marked as untrusted.

Passt is operated by Genesis Technologies FlexCo, Vienna, Austria.
capabilities: See discount codes a store has published
defaultPrompt: Find wool runners under $120 and check for a discount code.
What was added to the catalog this week?
Show me the newest in-stock products from Alo Yoga.

positive.expected_behavior: Returns matching products with title, listed price, availability and a link to the store's own page; the listed-price note says shipping and tax are set at the store's checkout. Says whether a discount code was found.

positive.prompt: What was added to the catalog this week?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists recently seen products with title, listed price and store link, and says it is recency in the index, not sales or popularity.

positive.prompt: Show me the newest in-stock products from aloyoga.com.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the search with the store, newest order and in-stock only, and lists only that store's products.

positive.prompt: Which stores with a UCP profile have the best uptime?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists stores with their host, product count and measured uptime, healthiest first.

positive.description: Search one store with a price bound
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the search with the store, a query and a price bound, and lists the matching products with their listed prices.
Before searching, asks one short round of neutral questions (for whom, colour, size, budget, delivery country). After the answer it calls the search with those filters and shows the offers card.

positive.prompt: Black women's pullover in size M under 60 euros, delivered to Austria.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the search with size M, a budget in EUR and Austria as the destination. The card shows offers that list size M first and marks offers whose size is not confirmed; prices are in EUR.

negative.prompt: Buy the wool runners for me.
Show my account balance and past orders.

review.commerce_description: Read-only product discovery. Nothing is sold or paid inside ChatGPT, and no result contains a payment link of ours. Each result links to the store's own website, where a person buys from that store (an external checkout the store operates); some links are affiliate links and are marked.

publication.release_notes: New offers card: up to eight products in a swipeable carousel, cheapest first within comparable offers, with larger pictures and the store's listed clothing and shoe sizes. New optional search inputs: size (clothing or shoe size; offers listing that size come first, unknown sizes stay visible and are marked) and askedForOptions. For a bare product type the assistant first asks one short round of neutral questions; for partly specified requests it shows offers and may ask one short follow-up. Hosts without cards get the offers as text. Same server URL, same read-only behaviour, no new tools.
